svg.text: A chain: the article builds, step by step, from a flaw in the old wiring-diagram model of the brain through
oscillation-based mechanisms to a wave theory of cognition, then uses that theory to explain analog computation
and finally consciousness itself — each stage resting on the one above it.

g.text: From fixed wiring to wave-based mind
Down the page is the article's own order: a problem with the classical model leads to oscillations and ephaptic
coupling, which feed a wave-based control theory, which explains moving brain states and analog computing, which
together are used to explain consciousness and unconsciousness.

g.title: Fixed-wiring model can't explain it — a third of neurons fire on any task — Classic feedforward, specialist-neuron models cannot explain why so many prefrontal neurons respond to almost every task. — → spya-k046f6
g.text: a third of neurons fire on any task

g.title: Neurons multitask (mixed selectivity) — same neuron, different meaning by context — Many cortical neurons blend sensory, motor and context signals, so a fixed synaptic map can't be the whole story. — → spya-v0gbwq
g.text: same neuron, different meaning by context

g.title: Brain waves organize and route spikes — Oscillations segregate and time spiking, and gate which regions can talk to which. — → spya-jnp59d
Waves push spikes directly (ephaptic coupling) — Electric fields alter nearby neurons' voltage without using a synapse, fast and over a wide area. — → spya-mapqhv
Alpha/beta waves as inhibitory 'stencils' — Spatial patterns of alpha/beta suppress gamma-driven spiking in some places, letting it through elsewhere. — → spya-qck2sw
Explains mixed selectivity and subspace coding — → spya-zmknun
Moving waves shift neural coding states — Traveling alpha/beta waves accompany the brain switching from one activity pattern to another. — → spya-y09vju
Wave interference = analog computation — Overlapping waves add, cancel and combine, doing math in parallel without digital steps. — → spya-h5qjz4
Far more energy-efficient than digital — → spya-szhg6f
Anesthesia disrupts wave organization, not specific cells — Very different drugs all converge on the same slow, desynchronized cortical waves when consciousness is lost. — → spya-uvev07
Synapses store, waves decide what's active now — → spya-dnv2tp
Vs. Global Workspace, IIT, Higher-Order theories — → spya-xn7mdj

g.text: A hub: the central idea (alpha/beta waves as stencils that suppress or permit gamma spiking) has three things it is
used to explain, shown as satellites rather than a strict sequence.

g.title: Alpha/beta as inhibitory stencils — push-pull with gamma spiking — Spatially patterned alpha/beta rhythms suppress gamma-driven spiking in some cortical locations while sparing others, routing information without the brain needing to track specific synapses. — → spya-qck2sw

Alpha/beta's millimeter scale fits top-down control — confirmed in primate PFC — Gamma is too fine-grained, theta/delta too broad; alpha/beta sits at the right spatial scale, and in primates it does encode context and predicts errors. — → spya-azz3c8

Produces mixed selectivity — no dedicated 'context neurons' needed — A neuron inside the stencil in one context but outside it in another looks like it has switched its tuning, without any fixed context-detecting cells. — → spya-zmknun

Produces orthogonal subspace coding — reconciles noisy cells, tidy populations — The stencils split spiking into separate, structured subsets of active neurons, which is what low-dimensional 'subspace' coding looks like. — → spya-m63zb9

g.text: Inside: Traveling Waves and Analog Computation
A chain: moving waves are shown to drive state changes, which is then reframed as a form of computation, which is
argued to be efficient and used for combining task contexts.

g.title: Beta waves travel across motor cortex before/after movement — Beta rhythms, which brake movement, rise and fall as a moving wave timed to movement onset and offset. — → spya-qr9ra4
g.text: Beta waves travel across motor cortex

g.title: Traveling waves may drive switches between coding states — Moving patterns of inhibition/excitation could transition population activity from one orthogonal subspace to another. — → spya-mrsvfu
Analog computing: continuous physical quantities do the math — Instead of binary signals, waves directly add, cancel and combine — the physics itself performs the calculation. — → spya-vp5h33

Whole pattern settles at once, all in parallel — far cheaper than step-by-step digital logic — Because the medium evolves everywhere simultaneously, analog wave computation is inherently parallel and energy-efficient. — → spya-mgnqxk
g.text: Whole pattern settles at once, all in
far cheaper than step-by-step digital logic

g.title: Example: summing two context-waves gives a unique pattern per combination — Two task-context signals, each a wave pattern, sum to produce a distinct neural pattern for every combination of contexts — an 'intersection of constraints.' — → spya-prykb8
g.text: gives a unique pattern per combination
